sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'Phonemics and Phonology' (pp. 22-42) covers segments, vowel length, a binary H/L tone contrast (p. 24, p. 34), syllable structure and morphophonemics; transcriptions are segmental only because recordings 'were not ideal for tonological analyses' (p. 34). No mention of stress, accent, penultimate prominence or lengthening anywhere in the grammar (a full-text search for stress/accent).

sources.note: Nothing on accent. Typewritten scan (no text layer; pages read as images): p. 3 tone-marking conventions (low marked, high unmarked, falling, rising); ch. I morphophonologie verbale pp. 4-10, with 'morphotonologie' pp. 8-10: 'Le systeme tonal de l'ikyaushi est complexe et apparemment irregulier' (p. 9), tone shift, tone harmony, tonal contrast. Treats the language as tonal.
